+    def _passages(self, content: str) -> list[str]:

+        Decoded windows are used only for relevance scoring. Generation and grounding

+        if len(tokens) <= size:
+            return [content]
+        stride = size - self.settings.reranker_passage_overlap
+        starts = list(range(0, max(1, len(tokens) - size + stride), stride))
+        limit = self.settings.reranker_max_passages

+# Microgrid PDF regression verification
+
+Verified on 15 September 2026 against the existing microgrid collection and the
+configured live embedding, reranking, and LLM providers, with answer caching disabled.
+
+## Diagnosis
+
+All four pages extracted completely into four page-preserving chunks. The original
+normal-range request rejected every candidate at the relevance threshold. The
+below-35% request selected only page 1, while the response procedure is on pages 2–3;
+the generator correctly returned empty claims for the incomplete context.
+
+## Changes
+
+- `src/providers/reranker.py`: score bounded overlapping passages and retain each
+  original chunk for generation/citations. Keep the configured relevance threshold.
+- `src/config.py` and `.env.example`: configurable passage length, overlap and count.
+- `src/rag/grounding.py`: clarify quoting operational procedures and PDF table rows.
+- `src/rag/pipeline.py`, `src/models/schemas.py`, `src/observability/events.py`, and
+  `src/ui/pages.py`: metadata-only abstention reasons and source/generation counts.
+- PDF regression fixture and tests; updated README and engineering decisions.
+
+The local web, worker and scheduler services were rebuilt and restarted. Existing
+collections and documents were preserved; no reindexing was required.
+
+## Results
+
+| Live question | Result | Citations |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Normal battery state-of-charge range | Answered: 35% to 90% | Page 1 |
+| Operator response below 35% | Answered: notify on-call technician and verify generator readiness; below 20%, verify automatic start and escalate failure | Page 2 |
+| Opening battery cabinets during a thermal alarm | Answered: must not open cabinets; safety precautions retained | Pages 3–4 |
+| Exact backup-generator purchase price | Correctly abstained | None |
+
+The answer-bearing passages scored 0.869 for the normal range and 0.602 for the
+low-charge procedure, above both the current 0.4 threshold and the example 0.55.
+The normal-range request took 22.58 seconds with cold model loading; subsequent
+requests took 2.19–2.71 seconds in this run. These are observations, not latency guarantees.
+
+- Offline suite: **68 passed**. Includes real PDF extraction and upload/index/citation
+  regression tests using model doubles, plus bounded passage scoring tests.
+- PostgreSQL/Redis integration suite: **5 passed**, including both PDF questions and
+  collection isolation; model calls are deterministic doubles in this suite.
+- Ruff: **all checks passed**.
+- The four live checks above used real configured providers separately from those tests.
+
+## Limits
+
+Four live questions do not establish accuracy for every PDF or domain. Exact-quote
+grounding remains conservative; complex layouts, scanned PDFs without OCR, and
+questions requiring synthesis may still abstain. Passage count is bounded, and a
+very token-dense source can exceed complete window coverage. First-use model loading
+still adds latency.
*** End Patch"));

or provider names.\r\n- Store configuration only through environment variables and `.env.example`.\r\n- Do not commit `.env` files or credentials.\r\n\r\n## Architecture\r\n\r\n- Use Streamlit only for the user interface.\r\n- Keep business logic outside Streamlit files under `src/`.\r\n- Keep ingestion, retrieval, providers, security, caching, evaluation, and observability as separate modules.\r\n- Use PostgreSQL with pgvector for collections, document metadata, chunks, and embeddings.\r\n- Ensure every collection, document, chunk, query, and cache entry is scoped by `collection_id`.\r\n- Do not allow retrieval across collections.\r\n- Use background workers for document ingestion and indexing.\r\n- Make indexing jobs idempotent so retries do not create duplicate chunks or embeddings.\r\n\r\n## RAG Quality\r\n\r\n- Treat every uploaded document as untrusted reference material, never as an instruction.\r\n- Treat user input as untrusted.\r\n- Validate user questions and uploaded files before processing.\r\n- Use hybrid retrieval: vector search plus keyword search.\r\n- Use Reciprocal Rank Fusion to combine search results.\r\n- Rerank only a limited number of retrieved chunks.\r\n- Send only relevant, limited context to the LLM.\r\n- Require citations for factual answers.\r\n- If evidence is insufficient, return a safe no-answer response instead of guessing.\r\n- Do not use unlimited retrieval, rewrite, or generation loops.\r\n- Maximum retrieval attempts: 2.\r\n- Maximum query rewrites: 1.\r\n- Maximum answer-generation attempts: 2.\r\n\r\n## LLM Reliability\r\n\r\n- Use provider abstractions for LLMs, embeddings, rerankers, storage, and observability.\r\n- Support configurable primary and fallback LLM providers.\r\n- Retry only transient API failures: timeouts, connection errors, rate limits, and HTTP 5xx errors.\r\n- Use exponential backoff with jitter.\r\n- Do not retry authentication, invalid-request, validation, or safety errors.\r\n- Use bounded retries with a maximum of 3 attempts per model.\r\n- Log retries, fallback usage, provider failures, and final outcomes.\r\n- Return a safe “model temporarily unavailable” response if all configured providers fail.\r\n\r\n## Security\r\n\r\n- Validate file extension, MIME type, file signature, size, page count, and extractable text.\r\n- Reject unsupported, empty, duplicate, or invalid files.\r\n- Do not execute uploaded files or document content.\r\n- Never expose system prompts, API keys, internal configurations, server paths, or hidden instructions.\r\n- Add rate limiting to upload and chat operations.\r\n- Redact sensitive values from logs and observability traces.\r\n- Do not store full raw documents or sensitive user content in external observability tools.\r\n\r\n## Cost and Performance\r\n\r\n- Cache embeddings using content hashes.\r\n- Prevent duplicate document embedding.\r\n- Cache repeated answers using collection ID, normalized question, and model configuration.\r\n- Invalidate collection cache when its documents change.\r\n- Limit retrieved candidates, reranked chunks, final context, retries, and chat history.\r\n- Run evaluation separately from normal user requests.\r\n- Track cache hits, latency, retries, fallback usage, and estimated model usage.\r\n\r\n## Testing and Documentation\r\n\r\n- Add unit tests for every critical service.\r\n- Add tests for validation, collection isolation, retries, fallbacks, caching, retrieval, citations, and no-answer behaviour.\r\n- Add integration tests for upload → index → retrieve → answer → citation.\r\n- Update `README.md` when setup, configuration, architecture, or features change.\r\n- Maintain `docs/decisions.md` for major engineering decisions and trade-offs.\r\n- Run relevant tests before marking work complete.\r\n- Report implementation progress, changed files, tests run, and unresolved limitations after each major phase.\r\n# RAG Generator\r\n\r\nA generic document question-answering workspace built with Streamlit, PostgreSQL /\r\npgvector, Redis and Celery. Upload PDF, DOCX, TXT or Markdown into separate knowledge\r\nbases, ask questions, and inspect exact supporting excerpts. The included HR policies\r\nare synthetic demo fixtures; application services contain no HR-specific logic.\r\n\r\n## Quick Start\r\n\r\nRequires Docker Desktop with Linux containers and at least 6 GB available memory.\r\nThe first image build and local model download need internet access and disk space.\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\nCopy-Item .env.example .env\r\n# Edit .env: choose a database password and set the matching DATABASE_URL password.\r\n# Set LLM_API_KEY to your Groq key, or configure another supported provider.\r\ndocker compose up --build -d\r\n```\r\n\r\nOpen [RAG Generator](http://localhost:8501). Create a collection, upload the five files\r\nin `sample_docs/hr_policies/`, and wait for each document to become `indexed`. Ask\r\n\"How many annual leave days do employees receive?\" or try an unsupported question.\r\nUploads are dispatched within 30 seconds. First indexing loads the local embedding\r\nmodel; the first question also loads the reranker. These first requests take longer.\r\n\r\nThis checkout has a locally generated, ignored `.env` for verification. It contains\r\nno LLM credentials. Preserve it when supplying your key; do not overwrite or commit it.\r\nThe default Ollama fallback requires a separately running Ollama server and the model\r\nspecified in `.env`. The app returns a safe unavailable response without a working LLM.\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\ndocker compose ps\r\ndocker compose logs --tail 50 worker\r\ndocker compose stop\r\n```\r\n\r\nStopping containers preserves documents and database volumes. `docker compose down -v`\r\npermanently deletes the project volumes; it is not a routine restart command.\r\n\r\n## Architecture\r\n\r\n```mermaid\r\nflowchart LR\r\n    UI[Streamlit] --> Services[Collection and question services]\r\n    Services --> PG[(PostgreSQL + pgvector)]\r\n    Services --> Files[Local object storage]\r\n    Services --> Redis[(Redis cache and broker)]\r\n    Beat[Celery scheduler] --> Jobs[Pending database jobs]\r\n    Jobs --> Workers[Celery worker]\r\n    Workers --> Extract[Validate / extract / chunk / embed]\r\n    Extract --> PG\r\n    Services --> Search[Vector + keyword / RRF / rerank]\r\n    Search --> Gate[Confidence gate]\r\n    Gate --> LLM[Primary / alternate model / fallback provider]\r\n    LLM --> Verify[Exact claims and citation validation]\r\n    Verify --> UI\r\n    Workers --> Eval[Separate evaluation run]\r\n    Services --> Logs[Metadata-only JSON / optional Langfuse]\r\n```\r\n\r\n- `src/ingestion/`: file validation, source extraction, token chunking, ingestion service.\r\n- `src/rag/`: scoped hybrid retrieval, bounded RAG orchestration and grounding checks.\r\n- `src/providers/`: LLM, embedding, reranker, storage and observability contracts/adapters.\r\n- `src/security/`, `src/cache/`, `src/observability/`: separate cross-cutting services.\r\n- `src/evaluation/`: metrics and evaluation orchestration; `evals/` holds fixtures and CLI.\r\n- `src/ui/`: Streamlit presentation only. `app.py` composes navigation.\r\n- `src/migrate.py`: serialized, versioned database bootstrap; add numbered migrations\r\n  for subsequent schema changes. Existing schema versions are never recreated.\r\n- `worker/`: Celery tasks and durable pending-job dispatcher.\r\n\r\nCollection/document composite foreign keys prevent mismatched chunk ownership. Every\r\nsearch and mutation takes `collection_id`. Advisory locks serialize duplicate job\r\ndelivery; atomic chunk publication increments the collection revision. Revision-aware\r\ncache keys prevent stale answers after indexing or deletion. Model fingerprints stop\r\nmixing incompatible embedding spaces. See [decisions](docs/decisions.md) and the\r\n[implementation plan](docs/implementation-plan.md) for trade-offs and phase checks.\r\n\r\n## Configuration\r\n\r\nAll deployment choices are read through environment variables / `.env`; `.env.example`\r\nis the complete reference. Never place credentials in source code or commit `.env`.\r\n\r\n| Variables | Purpose |\r\n| --- | --- |\r\n| `LLM_PROVIDER`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY` | Primary provider |\r\n| `LLM_SAME_PROVIDER_FALLBACK_MODEL` | Optional alternate model on the primary endpoint |\r\n| `LLM_FALLBACK_PROVIDER`, `LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL`, `LLM_FALLBACK_BASE_URL`, `LLM_FALLBACK_API_KEY` | Optional alternate provider |\r\n| `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER`, `EMBEDDING_MODEL`, `EMBEDDING_DIMENSION` | Local or Gemini embeddings |\r\n| `EMBEDDING_BASE_URL`, `EMBEDDING_API_KEY` | Gemini embedding endpoint and credential |\r\n| `RERANKER_PROVIDER`, `RERANKER_MODEL`, `MODEL_DEVICE` | Local cross-encoder deployment |\r\n| `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL` | Local development connections; Compose sets container hosts |\r\n| `POSTGRES_PORT`, `REDIS_PORT`, `APP_PORT` | Loopback host ports (55432, 56379, 8501 in example) |\r\n| `STORAGE_ROOT`, `RESULTS_ROOT` | Local runtime storage roots |\r\n| `MAX_UPLOAD_MB`, `MAX_PAGES`, `MAX_EXTRACTED_CHARACTERS` | Extraction limits |\r\n| `STREAMLIT_THEME_BASE`, `STREAMLIT_THEME_PRIMARY_COLOR`, `STREAMLIT_THEME_BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `STREAMLIT_THEME_SECONDARY_BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `STREAMLIT_THEME_TEXT_COLOR` | Native UI theme; Compose defaults to a white/slate workspace with blue actions |\r\n| `MIN_RERANK_SCORE` | Calibrate for your chosen cross-encoder and documents |\r\n| `OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED`, `LANGFUSE_HOST`, `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` | Optional metadata-only external tracing |\r\n| `EVAL_ENABLE_RAGAS`, `EVAL_LLM_MODEL`, `EVAL_LLM_BASE_URL`, `EVAL_LLM_API_KEY` | Explicit opt-in evaluation judge |\r\n\r\nProvider IDs are `groq`, `gemini`, and `ollama`; embedding IDs are `local` and `gemini`.\r\nGroq expects an OpenAI-compatible base URL ending in `/openai/v1`, Gemini a REST base\r\nending in `/v1beta`, and Ollama its server origin. These values and model names are\r\nexamples, not availability guarantees. Gemini embedding dimensions must match the\r\nreturned model dimension. To change the embedding model, create and upload into a\r\nnew collection; incompatible existing collections are rejected with a clear message.\r\n\r\n## Grounding and Reliability\r\n\r\nThe pipeline retrieves at most 20 vector and 20 keyword candidates, combines them\r\nusing RRF, reranks at most 10, and sends at most 4-6 selected chunks within a token\r\nbudget. Chunk targets are 600 tokens with 100 overlap, bounded to 450-700 and 80-120;\r\nshort structural sections remain short to preserve page/heading provenance.\r\nFor example, the four-page microgrid PDF produces four complete page chunks; a low\r\nchunk count does not imply missing text. Reranking scores overlapping passages within\r\neach chunk using the reranker's tokenizer (180 tokens, 40 overlap, at most 16 passages\r\nper candidate), then uses the highest passage score. Original chunks remain intact\r\nfor generation and citations. Configure these bounds with `RERANKER_PASSAGE_TOKENS`,\r\n`RERANKER_PASSAGE_OVERLAP`, and `RERANKER_MAX_PASSAGES`; when capped, windows are spread\r\nacross the source. Existing collections benefit immediately without reindexing.\r\n\r\nWeak evidence permits one query rewrite and a second retrieval. Answer generation\r\npermits one retry after citation validation fails. Each LLM operation tries at most\r\nthree attempts per configured model, with exponential backoff and jitter only for\r\ntimeouts, network failures, HTTP 429 and HTTP 5xx. Authentication and invalid requests\r\nare not retried on the same model. Safety refusals stop fallback. Redis-backed circuit\r\nstate suppresses models after repeated failed operations until the cooldown expires.\r\n\r\nVersion 1 accepts exact source passages, not arbitrary paraphrases. It rejects unknown\r\nchunk IDs, changed quotes, cross-collection evidence, obvious document instructions,\r\nand partial sentences that strip leading negations. This reduces unsupported answers\r\nbut can abstain on valid questions requiring synthesis. Confidence is a heuristic\r\nderived from reranker scores, not a calibrated probability or a truth guarantee.\r\nOperator procedures and complete PDF table rows may be quoted as evidence, while\r\ninstructions addressed to the assistant remain untrusted. Request details distinguish\r\nmissing relevant evidence from a model response without valid supported claims.\r\n\r\nEmbedding caches use collection/model/content hashes. Answer caches include collection\r\nrevision, normalized question, bounded history and configuration fingerprint. Only\r\ngrounded answers are cached. History and cache values remain in local Redis with TTL;\r\nhistory is limited per collection and is treated as untrusted prompt data.\r\n\r\n## Evaluation\r\n\r\nFor the microgrid PDF, a dedicated [10-case evaluation dataset](evals/microgrid_dataset.md)\r\ncovers eight supported questions and two no-answer questions. Set\r\n`EVAL_DATASET_PATH=./evals/microgrid_dataset.json` and `EVAL_MAX_QUESTIONS=10`, recreate\r\nthe app services, then select the microgrid collection and use **Evaluation → Run evaluation**.\r\n\r\nThe default benchmark dataset (`evals/dataset.json`) is optimized for free-tier API quotas (10 questions across all 5 HR policy documents and all question categories: direct, multi-source, cross-document, ambiguous and unanswerable, plus ten explicit security fixtures). The comprehensive 36-question benchmark is preserved in `evals/dataset_full.json`. Request pacing (`EVAL_REQUEST_DELAY_SECONDS`) and bounded batch size (`EVAL_MAX_QUESTIONS`) prevent burst rate limit violations during live evaluation.\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m evals.run_eval --offline\r\npython -m evals.run_eval --collection-id <collection-uuid>\r\n```\r\n\r\nThe offline command needs no API key or running infrastructure. It measures a TF-IDF\r\nbaseline against filename/heading labels, plus deterministic security checks. It does\r\nnot claim to measure the real embedding/reranking/LLM system. The live command and\r\nStreamlit Evaluation page use the selected indexed collection and all five sample HR\r\nfiles. Evaluation is queued separately from chat, and results are scoped in PostgreSQL.\r\n\r\nMeasured offline result: Recall@5 **1.0000**, MRR@10 **1.0000**, explicit security fixture\r\npass rate **1.0000**. These small synthetic fixtures are not an adversarial benchmark.\r\nSee [the actual report](evals/results/latest_report.md) for timings and unmeasured metrics.\r\n\r\nLive reports include citation accuracy, lexical answer relevance, independently checked\r\nexact-excerpt support, no-answer precision, P50/P95 latency, cache hits and LLM calls.\r\nErrors/unavailable responses are not counted as successful abstentions. Null means\r\nunmeasured, not zero. Retrieval labels identify relevant filename/heading pairs.\r\n\r\nOptional Ragas evaluation:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m pip install -r requirements-eval.txt\r\n# Configure EVAL_* and set EVAL_ENABLE_RAGAS=true in .env, then run the live CLI.\r\n```\r\n\r\nRagas measures semantic faithfulness and reference-context recall with a separately\r\nconfigured judge. It is off by default and never runs on normal chat calls.\r\nThe base Docker image omits this optional dependency set; use the local CLI or install\r\nit in an explicitly extended evaluation image.\r\n\r\n## Development and Tests\r\n\r\nThe UI uses Streamlit's native theme for consistent inputs, dropdowns, tables and\r\nstatus messages. `src/ui/styles.css` adds spacing, selected navigation and keyboard\r\nfocus treatment using theme colors, so switching to dark mode remains readable.\r\nTheme overrides belong in environment variables / `.env`, as shown in `.env.example`.\r\nCompose applies them on startup; after changing them, recreate the web container.\r\nFor a local Streamlit launch, load just the theme values from `.env.example` (or your\r\ncustomized `.env`) before starting Streamlit:\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\nGet-Content .env.example | ForEach-Object {\r\n    if ($_ -match '^(STREAMLIT_THEME_[A-Z_]+)=(.*)$') {\r\n        [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable($Matches[1], $Matches[2].Trim('\"'), 'Process')\r\n    }\r\n}\r\n```\r\n\r\n```powershell\r\npython -m venv venv\r\nvenv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1\r\npython -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt\r\npython -m src.migrate\r\npython -m pytest -q\r\npython -m ruff check .\r\nstreamlit run app.py\r\n```\r\n\r\nRun workers through Compose on Windows; Celery prefork is intended for Linux. Verification details and\r\nscreenshots are recorded in [verification](docs/verification.md).\r\n\r\n## Security and Deployment Limits\r\n\r\nThis is a production-minded assessment implementation, not an authenticated hosted\r\nservice. Default ports bind to localhost. Collections separate retrieval data but do\r\nnot authenticate or authorize users. Session rate limits can be bypassed by opening\r\nnew sessions; add identity-bound global limits and authorization before public use.\r\n\r\nExtension, MIME, signature, size, page indicators and extractable text are validated.\r\nDOCX archives are expansion-bounded, macros/embedded objects are rejected, and XML\r\nexternal entities are disabled. Scanned and encrypted PDFs are rejected with actionable\r\nmessages. DOCX page numbers rely on stored page breaks/metadata, not a layout engine;\r\nPDF headings may be unavailable. Adversarial PDF extraction still needs OS-level\r\nmemory/CPU isolation and malware scanning before exposure to untrusted internet users.\r\n\r\nDocuments are always evidence, never instructions. Keyword injection detection is a\r\nflagging layer alongside role separation, no tools, limited context and exact citation\r\nchecks. It does not guarantee resistance to every obfuscated attack or poisoned source.\r\nApplication telemetry allowlists metadata and excludes raw documents, questions,\r\nanswers, filenames, secrets and exception messages. Recent errors shown in the UI\r\nare process-local; use structured container logs for worker failures.\r\n\r\nExact vector search favors correctness for assessment-sized corpora. Add per-model\r\nHNSW indexes, authorization/RLS, backups, TLS, parser isolation, dedicated evaluation\r\nworkers and deployment-specific resource limits before scaling. Local models may\r\ndownload weights at first use; provision model caches in offline deployments. Large\r\nchunks are embedded in model-token windows and pooled to avoid silent truncation.\r\nReranking uses bounded passage windows to reduce dilution and avoid dropping the end\r\nof ordinary chunks. +# RAG Generator
+
+A document question-answering workspace with separate knowledge bases, hybrid retrieval, cited answers, and an explicit evaluation workflow. Upload PDF, DOCX, TXT, or Markdown documents, ask questions about the selected collection, and inspect the supporting source excerpts.
+
+Built with **Python 3.11+, Streamlit, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Redis, and Celery**. Streamlit handles presentation; ingestion, retrieval, model providers, security, caching, and evaluation live in separate service modules.
+
+The application produces extractive answers: it quotes supported passages and abstains when it cannot establish enough evidence. It is designed for a trusted local workspace; authentication and public multi-user hosting are not implemented.
+
+![Knowledge Bases dashboard with an indexed microgrid PDF](images/kb_dashboard.png)
+
+## Contents
+
+- [Features](#features)
+- [Architecture](#architecture)
+- [How the RAG pipeline works](#how-the-rag-pipeline-works)
+- [Quick start with Docker](#quick-start-with-docker)
+- [Using the application](#using-the-application)
+- [Configuration](#configuration)
+- [Evaluation](#evaluation)
+- [Application screenshots](#application-screenshots)
+- [Development and testing](#development-and-testing)
+- [Operations and persistence](#operations-and-persistence)
+- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
+- [Security and data handling](#security-and-data-handling)
+- [Known limitations](#known-limitations)
+- [Project structure](#project-structure)
+- [Further documentation](#further-documentation)
+
+## Features
+
+| Capability | Implementation |
+| --- | --- |
+| Separate knowledge bases | Collection-scoped uploads, retrieval, caches, and evaluation results |
+| Document ingestion | Validation, text extraction, page/heading metadata, token chunking, background indexing |
+| Hybrid search | pgvector cosine search plus PostgreSQL English full-text search, combined with Reciprocal Rank Fusion |
+| Passage reranking | Local cross-encoder scores overlapping passages within each candidate chunk |
+| Grounded answers | Structured model output, source-ID validation, supporting quotes, page/heading citations |
+| Safe outcomes | Distinct answered, abstained, rejected, and temporarily unavailable responses |
+| Model reliability | Configurable primary and fallback LLMs, bounded transient retries, shared circuit state |
+| Cost controls | Embedding and answer caches; bounded retrieval, context, history, generation, and evaluation |
+| Evaluation | Collection-specific datasets, retrieval/citation/abstention metrics, optional RAGAS judge |
+| Operational visibility | Request details, service checks, metadata-only application events, optional Langfuse |
+
+The included HR documents and microgrid guide are sample/reference fixtures. The application itself is not restricted to either domain.
+
+## Architecture
+
+### Services and dependencies
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TB
+    Browser["Browser"] --> Web["Streamlit web service"]
+    Web --> Services["Python application services"]
+    Services --> PG[("PostgreSQL + pgvector")]
+    Services --> Files[("Uploaded files")]
+    Services --> Redis[("Redis: broker, caches, rate limits, circuits")]
+    Services --> RAG["RAG pipeline"]
+    RAG --> PG
+    RAG --> Embeddings["Embedding provider: local or remote"]
+    RAG --> Reranker["Local cross-encoder"]
+    RAG --> LLM["Primary LLM and configured fallbacks"]
+    Beat["Celery Beat: every 30 seconds"] --> Redis
+    Redis --> Worker["Celery worker: ingestion and evaluation queues"]
+    Worker --> PG
+    Worker --> Files
+    Worker --> Embeddings
+    Worker --> Eval["Evaluation service"]
+    Eval --> RAG
+    Eval -. "Optional" .-> Judge["RAGAS judge endpoint"]
+    Services --> Telemetry["Metadata-only application telemetry"]
+    Worker --> Telemetry
+    Telemetry --> Logs["Structured JSON logs"]
+    Telemetry -. "Optional" .-> Langfuse["Langfuse"]
+```
+
+The database is the durable source of job status. The scheduler sends a dispatcher task through Redis; the worker reads pending database jobs and queues ingestion/evaluation tasks. Uploading a document or requesting an evaluation does not run that expensive work in the Streamlit page.
+
+| Compose service | Responsibility |
+| --- | --- |
+| `web` | Streamlit application and synchronous question answering |
+| `worker` | Document indexing and evaluation; one worker process by default, consuming both queues |
+| `scheduler` | Celery Beat dispatcher schedule and recovery of pending work |
+| `migrate` | One-shot, versioned database bootstrap and pgvector/full-text setup |
+| `db` | PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector |
+| `redis` | Celery broker, caches, rate limits, and LLM circuit counters |
+
+Database and Redis health checks gate service startup. `migrate` must complete before the application services start. A successfully exited migration container is normal.
+
+### Data model and isolation
+
+| Entity | Stored information |
+| --- | --- |
+| Collection | UUID, name, revision, embedding-configuration fingerprint |
+| Document | Collection UUID, filename, MIME type, content hash, storage key, status, attempts, chunk count |
+| Chunk | Collection/document UUIDs, source text, page, heading, ordinal, content hash, vector |
+| Evaluation run | Collection UUID, run UUID, status, report JSON, error code |
+
+Raw files are stored under collection/document UUID paths in shared file storage. Document metadata, chunks, embeddings, and evaluation results are stored in PostgreSQL. Redis caches are disposable and are not the durable document store. Conversation history lives in the Streamlit session; bounded history may also be present in cached answers' surrounding application state, but no chat-history database table is implemented.
+
+Every retrieval query filters by `collection_id` and indexed-document status. Composite foreign keys prevent assigning a chunk to a document from another collection. Duplicate content within a collection is rejected, and indexing atomically publishes chunks while incrementing the collection revision. The embedding fingerprint prevents using a collection with an incompatible embedding configuration.
+
+## How the RAG pipeline works
+
+### 1. Validate and index documents
+
+```mermaid
+sequenceDiagram
+    actor User
+    participant UI as Streamlit
+    participant Ingest as Ingestion service
+    participant Store as File storage
+    participant DB as PostgreSQL
+    participant Jobs as Scheduler and worker
+    participant Embed as Cached embedding provider
+    User->>UI: Upload into selected collection
+    UI->>Ingest: Validate file and collection
+    Ingest->>Ingest: Extract text and reject invalid/duplicate content
+    Ingest->>Store: Store bytes under UUID key
+    Ingest->>DB: Create pending document
+    Ingest-->>UI: Queued
+    Jobs->>DB: Discover pending work and acquire document lock
+    Jobs->>Store: Read uploaded file
+    Jobs->>Jobs: Revalidate, extract, and chunk text
+    Jobs->>Embed: Reuse cached embeddings or compute vectors
+    Jobs->>DB: Atomically publish chunks; mark indexed; increment revision
+    UI->>DB: Refresh document status
+```
+
+Validation checks extension, MIME type, file signature, size, page limits where available, and usable extracted text. Password-protected PDFs and documents without usable text are rejected. There is no built-in OCR. DOCX validation also bounds archive expansion and rejects macros and embedded objects.
+
+Chunking preserves page/heading boundaries and uses the configured tiktoken encoding. The example target is **600 tokens with 100-token overlap**; short sections remain shorter. Paragraph boundaries are preferred where possible. PDF headings are not generally inferred from visual typography, and table cells can appear as consecutive extracted lines.
+
+The four-page microgrid fixture correctly produces **four page chunks** at the example settings. A small chunk count alone does not indicate missing text.
+
+Indexing uses advisory locks, unique constraints, and atomic publication to make repeated delivery idempotent. Already indexed documents are skipped. Failed recoverable jobs have bounded attempts; the UI's **Retry** action resets a failed document for another attempt.
+
+### 2. Retrieve and answer a question
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TD
+    Q["Question and selected collection"] --> Validate["Rate limit, validate question, check embedding fingerprint"]
+    Validate --> Cache{"Valid answer cache hit?"}
+    Cache -->|Yes| Cached["Return cached cited answer"]
+    Cache -->|No| Embed["Embed search query"]
+    Embed --> Vector["Scoped vector search"]
+    Embed --> Keyword["Scoped keyword search"]
+    Vector --> RRF["Reciprocal Rank Fusion"]
+    Keyword --> RRF
+    RRF --> Rerank["Score bounded passages; rank original chunks"]
+    Rerank --> Gate["Relevance and injection checks; context budget"]
+    Gate --> Evidence{"Usable evidence?"}
+    Evidence -->|"No: first retrieval"| Rewrite["One query rewrite"]
+    Rewrite --> Embed
+    Evidence -->|"No: second retrieval"| Abstain["Safe no-answer response"]
+    Evidence -->|Yes| Generate["Generate structured claims using reliable LLM"]
+    Generate --> Ground{"Claims and citations valid?"}
+    Ground -->|"No: first generation"| Repair["One stricter generation attempt"]
+    Repair --> Generate
+    Ground -->|"No: second generation"| Abstain
+    Ground -->|Yes| Revision{"Collection revision unchanged?"}
+    Revision -->|Yes| Answer["Return answer with citations; cache grounded result"]
+    Revision -->|No| Abstain
+```
+
+**Hybrid retrieval.** Vector search orders chunks by cosine distance. Keyword search uses PostgreSQL's English `to_tsvector`/`plainto_tsquery` and `ts_rank_cd`. RRF combines rankings using `sum(1 / (60 + rank))`, deduplicated by chunk UUID. Vector and keyword scores are not directly averaged.
+
+**Reranking.** The cross-encoder scores overlapping passages using its own tokenizer. Each original chunk receives its highest passage score, transformed with a sigmoid. The example passage settings are **180 tokens, 40-token overlap, and at most 16 passages per candidate**. Generation and citation validation still receive the original text, preserving line breaks and provenance. When the passage budget is exceeded, sampled windows are spread across the source. This improves retrieval of facts inside longer PDF pages without reindexing existing collections.
+
+**Grounding.** The LLM must return JSON claims containing text, a source chunk UUID, and a supporting quote. The validator checks source membership, claim/quote agreement, source support, and unsafe content patterns. It permits whitespace-normalized matching as a fallback. It does not allow unrestricted paraphrasing or arbitrary synthesis. Operator procedures may be quoted as facts; document instructions addressed to the assistant remain untrusted.
+
+**Abstention.** Missing relevant evidence or a response without valid supported claims produces a safe no-answer response. A source that explicitly says a topic is unspecified may instead support a cited answer explaining that boundary. Confidence is a heuristic based on selected reranker scores, not a calibrated probability or a guarantee of correctness.
+
+### 3. Bound retries, context, and cost
+
+| Control | Example configuration or enforced limit |
+| --- | --- |
+| Vector / keyword candidates | 20 / 20 maximum |
+| Candidates sent to reranker | 10 maximum |
+| Selected context chunks | Up to 5 by default; configurable cap from 4 to 6, with fewer allowed when evidence is weak |
+| Context token budget | 3,500 by default |
+| Retrieval attempts / query rewrites | At most 2 / 1 |
+| Answer-generation attempts | At most 2 |
+| LLM attempts per configured model, per operation | At most 3 |
+| Output budget / history | 1,200 output tokens; up to 6 previous messages in the example |
+| Claims | At most 8 per generated answer |
+
+Transient LLM timeouts, connection failures, HTTP 429, and HTTP 5xx receive exponential backoff with jitter. Authentication, invalid-request, and other non-transient errors are not retried on the same model. Ordered fallback can then use an alternate model on the primary endpoint and an alternate provider. Safety refusals stop fallback. Redis circuit counters temporarily skip repeatedly failing providers. The LLM retry wrapper does not wrap every service call; embeddings and indexing have their own failure paths.
+
+Embedding cache keys include collection ID, embedding configuration, query/document purpose, and hashed content. Answer keys include collection ID, revision, normalized question, model/pipeline configuration, and bounded history. Only grounded answers are cached. Document changes advance the revision; deletion also clears collection caches. A repeated question with different chat history may therefore miss the answer cache.
+
+## Quick start with Docker
+
+### Prerequisites
+
+- Docker Desktop running Linux containers, or Docker Engine with the Compose plugin on Linux.
+- Internet access for the first image build, model downloads, and any configured remote providers.
+- Memory and disk space for PyTorch, model weights, PostgreSQL, and uploaded documents. Resource needs depend on the selected models; the supplied image uses CPU PyTorch.
+- A working LLM configuration: credentials for a supported remote provider or a reachable Ollama server with the configured model already available.
+
+Run the commands below from the repository root. The examples use PowerShell unless marked otherwise.
+
+### 1. Create the environment file
+
+```powershell
+Copy-Item .env.example .env
+```
+
+Do this only on first setup; preserve an existing `.env`. Edit the new file before starting services:
+
+1. Replace `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and use the same password in the host-side `DATABASE_URL`. URL-encode credentials containing URL-special characters in that URL.
+2. Set `LLM_API_KEY` for the example primary provider, or configure the primary provider/model/endpoint you intend to use.
+3. Review the example Ollama fallback. Run that server and model separately, or disable the alternate provider by setting `LLM_FALLBACK_PROVIDER=`.
+4. Choose local or remote embeddings. Remote embeddings require the matching endpoint, key, and output dimension.
+5. Choose the evaluation dataset for the documents you will upload; see [Evaluation](#evaluation).
+
+Provider IDs are implementation identifiers. Model names and endpoints in `.env.example` are configurable examples, not model-availability guarantees. Credentials belong only in environment configuration and must not be committed.
+
+### 2. Build and start
+
+```powershell
+docker compose up -d --build
+docker compose ps
+```
+
+Open [http://localhost:8501](http://localhost:8501), or the `APP_PORT` you configured. Compose overrides database/Redis URLs with container hostnames internally; host-side Python commands use the URLs in `.env`.
+
+First builds and model loads take longer. With local embeddings, the first indexing job loads an embedding model. The first question in each application process loads the reranker. The Docker model cache persists in the shared `app_data` volume.
+
+### 3. Load a sample collection
+
+For the microgrid workflow, create a collection and upload [microgrid_operations_and_response_guide.pdf](tests/fixtures/microgrid_operations_and_response_guide.pdf). Wait for `indexed`, then ask:
+
+- What is the normal battery state-of-charge range?
+- What should an operator do if battery state of charge falls below 35%?
+- What is the exact purchase price of the backup generator?
+
+The last question tests abstention because the guide does not specify that price.
+
+Alternatively, seed the synthetic HR collection:
+
+```powershell
+docker compose exec web python -m src.cli seed-demo
+```
+
+This queues the Markdown documents in `sample_docs/hr_policies/` and prints the collection UUID. Background dispatch occurs every 30 seconds; actual completion also depends on worker load and provider response time.
+
+## Using the application
+
+| Page | Workflow |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Knowledge Bases** | Create/select a collection, upload supported files, inspect indexing status and chunk counts, retry failed documents, delete documents or a collection |
+| **Ask Questions** | Ask about the selected collection, inspect confidence and timing, expand source citations and request details |
+| **Evaluation** | Queue a run using the configured dataset, choose a run, inspect summary metrics and question-result rows |
+| **System Status** | Check database/Redis readiness, worker availability, configured providers, model-loading state, and recent process-local errors |
+
+The sidebar collection selector controls document, chat, and evaluation scope. Document status refreshes every five seconds and evaluation status every ten seconds. Chat history is separate for each collection within the browser session.
+
+Request details distinguish no evidence passing relevance checks from a model response without valid supported claims. A temporary provider/service failure is reported as unavailable rather than as a successful no-answer result.
+
+## Configuration
+
+[.env.example](.env.example) lists deployment examples; [src/config.py](src/config.py) defines Pydantic validation and defaults. Example values below describe the template, not private local overrides.
+
+### Providers and infrastructure
+
+| Variables | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `LLM_PROVIDER`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_API_KEY` | Primary LLM; supported adapters: `groq`, `gemini`, `ollama` |
+| `LLM_SAME_PROVIDER_FALLBACK_MODEL` | Optional second model on the primary endpoint |
+| `LLM_FALLBACK_PROVIDER`, `LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL`, `LLM_FALLBACK_BASE_URL`, `LLM_FALLBACK_API_KEY` | Optional alternate provider |
+| `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER`, `EMBEDDING_MODEL`, `EMBEDDING_DIMENSION` | `local` or `gemini`; dimensions must match returned vectors |
+| `EMBEDDING_BASE_URL`, `EMBEDDING_API_KEY` | Remote embedding endpoint and credential |
+| `RERANKER_PROVIDER`, `RERANKER_MODEL`, `MODEL_DEVICE` | Local cross-encoder configuration; example device is `cpu` |
+| `TOKENIZER_ENCODING` | Tokenizer used for stored chunks and context budgeting |
+| `POSTGRES_DB`, `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | Database initialization credentials |
+| `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL` | Host-side service URLs; Compose supplies internal equivalents |
+| `POSTGRES_PORT`, `REDIS_PORT`, `APP_PORT` | Example loopback ports: 55432, 56379, 8501 |
+| `STORAGE_ROOT`, `RESULTS_ROOT` | Native file/report directories; Compose uses `/app/data/uploads` and `/app/data/evaluations` |
+
+The Groq adapter expects its chat API base ending in `/openai/v1`; Gemini adapters append model-specific REST paths to the configured base, typically ending in `/v1beta`; Ollama appends `/api/chat` to its server origin. The RAGAS judge uses a separate OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. Provider credentials are not interchangeable.
+
+For host Ollama accessed from a container, the template uses `host.docker.internal`. A host-native process should use a host-reachable origin instead. Ollama is not a service in this Compose file.
+
+Changing the embedding provider, model, dimension, or endpoint changes the collection fingerprint. Create a new collection and upload its documents using that configuration; the current UI does not offer in-place reindexing for an embedding-model change. Reranker-only changes do not require re-embedding.
+
+### Limits, caching, and observability
+
+| Variables | Example values / behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| `MAX_UPLOAD_MB`, `MAX_PAGES`, `MAX_EXTRACTED_CHARACTERS` | 20 MB, 100 pages, 2,000,000 extracted characters |
+| `CHUNK_TOKENS`, `CHUNK_OVERLAP` | 600 / 100; allowed ranges 450–700 / 80–120 |
+| `VECTOR_TOP_K`, `KEYWORD_TOP_K`, `RERANK_TOP_K` | 20 / 20 / 10 |
+| `RERANKER_PASSAGE_TOKENS`, `RERANKER_PASSAGE_OVERLAP`, `RERANKER_MAX_PASSAGES` | 180 / 40 / 16; overlap must be smaller than passage size |
+| `MIN_RERANK_SCORE` | 0.55; evaluate suitability for your model and documents |
+| `CONTEXT_TOP_K`, `MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS`, `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` | 5 / 3,500 / 1,200 |
+| `LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `LLM_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | 30 seconds per HTTP call / up to 3 attempts; not a total request deadline |
+| `CIRCUIT_FAILURE_THRESHOLD`, `CIRCUIT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` | 3 / 60 |
+| `CHAT_HISTORY_MESSAGES` | 6; zero disables history supplied to the pipeline |
+| `ANSWER_CACHE_TTL`, `EMBEDDING_CACHE_TTL` | 3,600 / 604,800 seconds |
+| `CHAT_RATE_LIMIT`, `UPLOAD_RATE_LIMIT`, `RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS` | 20 chat requests / 10 uploads per collection and session principal per 60-second window |
+| `OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED`, `LANGFUSE_HOST`, `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` | Optional metadata-only application tracing; disabled in the template |
+| `STREAMLIT_THEME_BASE`, `STREAMLIT_THEME_PRIMARY_COLOR`, `STREAMLIT_THEME_BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `STREAMLIT_THEME_SECONDARY_BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `STREAMLIT_THEME_TEXT_COLOR` | Native UI theme, applied to the web container by Compose |
+| `STREAMLIT_BROWSER_GATHER_USAGE_STATS` | Disabled in the Compose deployment |
+
+Evaluation settings and rebuild requirements are described below.
+
+## Evaluation
+
+Evaluation is explicit and separate from normal chat. UI runs are queued in PostgreSQL and processed by the Celery worker. CLI runs execute directly in the invoking process and do not create a dashboard run record.
+
+### Select a dataset
+
+| Dataset | Cases | Required collection |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| [HR dataset](evals/dataset.json) | 10 | The five indexed files in `sample_docs/hr_policies/` |
+| [Microgrid dataset](evals/microgrid_dataset.json) | 10: 8 answerable, 2 unanswerable | The indexed microgrid PDF, retaining its expected filename |
+| [Security fixtures](evals/security_dataset.json) | 10 | Validator checks, executed separately from the document questions |
+
+For the microgrid collection, set:
+
+```dotenv
+EVAL_DATASET_PATH=./evals/microgrid_dataset.json
+EVAL_MAX_QUESTIONS=10
+EVAL_REQUEST_DELAY_SECONDS=1.0
+```
+
+The selected dataset is global environment configuration, not automatically selected for each collection. Switch it when moving between HR and microgrid evaluations. A run checks that required filenames are indexed before issuing questions; a mismatch fails validation. The first `EVAL_MAX_QUESTIONS` cases are selected in file order. Pacing reduces bursts but does not guarantee compliance with provider quotas.
+
+Each case includes `id`, `question`, `category`, `expected_sources`, `reference`, and `answerable`. Source labels currently use `filename|heading`. PDF pages without extracted headings use `microgrid_operations_and_response_guide.pdf|None`. Unanswerable cases have an empty source list. See the [microgrid dataset guide](evals/microgrid_dataset.md) for page references and interpretation.
+
+### Run through the UI
+
+1. Apply dataset/configuration changes using the [rebuild instructions](#applying-changes).
+2. Select the matching knowledge base and confirm all required documents are `indexed`.
+3. Open **Evaluation** and click **Run evaluation** once.
+4. Wait for the selected run to change from `pending` to `processing` to `completed` or `failed`.
+5. Inspect summary metrics, latency charts, and **Question results**.
+
+The supplied worker handles ingestion and evaluation with concurrency one. A long evaluation can delay indexing. Completed report JSON is stored in PostgreSQL; the worker also writes a Markdown summary beneath `RESULTS_ROOT/<collection-id>/<run-id>.md`.
+
+### CLI alternatives
+
+These commands execute evaluations; they are not setup or health-check commands.
+
+Offline HR lexical baseline, with Python dependencies installed:
+
+```powershell
+python -m evals.run_eval --offline --output ./data/evaluations/hr-offline.md
+```
+
+The offline mode always uses the bundled HR Markdown files and default HR dataset. It does not use `EVAL_DATASET_PATH`, pgvector, a live embedding model, the cross-encoder, or an LLM. No running database or API key is required; it is a TF-IDF baseline plus deterministic security checks.
+
+Live collection evaluation inside Docker:
+
+```powershell
+$collectionId = "replace-with-your-collection-uuid"
+docker compose exec web python -m evals.run_eval --collection-id $collectionId --output /app/data/evaluations/manual-report.md
+```
+
+Use a real UUID, not the collection name. The seed command prints the demo collection UUID; for existing collections, a read-only listing is available through the repository:
+
+```powershell
+docker compose exec web python -c "from src.runtime import get_runtime; print('\n'.join(str(c.collection_id) + ' ' + c.name for c in get_runtime().repository.collections()))"
+```
+
+Live evaluation uses real configured providers and can consume API quota. It performs a retrieval/rerank measurement separately from `pipeline.ask`, so measured answer latency does not include the entire evaluation case. Answer caching remains enabled; report cache hits alongside latency when comparing runs.
+
+### Metrics and their limits
+
+| Metric | Meaning and interpretation |
+| --- | --- |
+| Recall@5 / MRR@10 | Relevant filename/heading labels in ranked retrieval results; not proof that final context or answers are correct |
+| Citation accuracy | Mean per-answer fraction of citations whose excerpts match stored content exactly and whose labels match expected sources |
+| Extractive faithfulness | Mean per-answer fraction of citations with exact stored-text support |
+| Lexical answer relevance | Case-insensitive exact reference substring in the answer; not a semantic judge |
+| No-answer precision | Truly unanswerable cases divided by all `abstained` cases; failures/unavailable responses are excluded |
+| P50 / P95 latency | Percentiles of pipeline answer latency; influenced by model loading, API responses, retries, and caching |
+| Cache hit rate / average LLM calls | Operational measurements from answer requests |
+| Security fixture pass rate | Deterministic pattern-validator checks; not a complete adversarial benchmark |
+
+`None` or **Not measured** means unavailable, not zero. PDF retrieval labels are document-level because multiple pages share the same filename and missing heading. The evaluator's exact citation checks are stricter about whitespace than the answer validator. A valid answer with normalized PDF line breaks can therefore receive a low citation score. Reference formatting and multi-passage answers can also depress the lexical metric.
+
+### Captured microgrid result
+
+The screenshots in this repository show one completed 10-case run, not a universal quality or performance guarantee:
+
+| Observation | Captured value |
+| --- | --- |
+| Recall@5 / MRR@10 | 100% / 1.0000 |
+| Citation accuracy / extractive faithfulness | Approximately 47.6% / 47.6% |
+| No-answer precision | 66.7% |
+| Answerable cases answered | 7 of 8; quarterly maintenance case `microgrid-08` abstained |
+| Unanswerable cases | Both abstained |
+| P50 / P95 answer latency | Approximately 2.18 / 10.20 seconds |
+
+The 66.7% value reflects two correct abstentions among three total abstentions. The retrieval labels and whitespace mismatch described above limit conclusions from the other percentages. Inspect question-level results before treating a score as an answer-quality measurement.
+
+### Optional RAGAS judge
+
+```dotenv
+EVAL_ENABLE_RAGAS=true
+EVAL_LLM_MODEL=your-judge-model
+EVAL_LLM_BASE_URL=your-openai-compatible-base-url
+EVAL_LLM_API_KEY=your-judge-key
+```
+
+RAGAS measures semantic faithfulness and reference-context recall using a separately configured judge. It sends questions, answers, retrieved context, and reference answers to that endpoint and can incur additional API usage. Enable it only for evaluations you intend to run. The implementation caps judge samples at ten and uses one judge worker.
+
+The **current Dockerfile installs `requirements-eval.txt`**, so rebuilding the supplied image includes RAGAS dependencies. Native installations need `python -m pip install -r requirements-eval.txt`. Judge execution is disabled in `.env.example`; installed dependencies alone do not enable it. A judge failure can leave the main evaluation report completed with a failed/skipped judge section; completion does not imply that semantic metrics were produced. The dashboard currently displays the core metrics, not the nested RAGAS result.

+## Development and testing
+
+### Host-side Python tools
+
+Use Python **3.11+**. Docker uses Python 3.11. From the repository root:
+
+```powershell
+python -m venv venv
+.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
+python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
+python -m pytest -q -m "not integration"
+python -m ruff check src tests worker evals app.py
+```
+
+If PowerShell activation is unavailable, invoke `.\venv\Scripts\python.exe` directly. Unit tests use provider doubles, but tiktoken may download its vocabulary on first use; warm that cache before offline execution. Test artifacts are configured under `data/` by `pyproject.toml`.
+
+Tests cover file/question validation, chunking, PDF extraction, collection isolation, model adapters, retry/fallback behavior, circuit state, caching, RRF, passage limits, grounding, no-answer behavior, evaluation metrics, and Streamlit navigation. The microgrid PDF fixture is exercised through upload, indexing, and citation tests.
+
+**Current checkout note:** `test_dataset_coverage` in `tests/test_evaluation.py` still refers to `evals/dataset_full.json`, which is absent from this checkout. That legacy fixture assertion must be updated or the intended fixture restored before the full suite can pass. The two shipped document datasets are listed above; the README does not assume a missing full benchmark exists.
+
+### PostgreSQL/Redis integration tests
+
+Start the infrastructure and apply the schema:
+
+```powershell
+docker compose up -d db redis
+python -m src.migrate
+$env:RUN_INTEGRATION = "1"
+python -m pytest -q -m integration
+Remove-Item Env:RUN_INTEGRATION
+```
+
+Host-side `DATABASE_URL` and `REDIS_URL` must match the published ports and actual credentials. Integration tests create unique collections and remove their own test data. They use real PostgreSQL/pgvector/Redis with deterministic model doubles, so they verify integration and isolation rather than live model quality.
+
+### Native application development
+
+For the complete native UI/worker workflow, use Linux or WSL and run all application processes from the same checkout with the same environment and storage paths. Keep PostgreSQL/Redis in Docker if desired. Avoid mixing a native uploader's file storage with workers that can only see Docker's named volume.
+
+After installing dependencies and running `python -m src.migrate`, start each process in a separate terminal with the virtual environment active:
+
+```bash
+# Terminal 1
+streamlit run app.py
+
+# Terminal 2
+celery -A worker.tasks:celery_app worker --loglevel=WARNING --concurrency=1 -Q ingestion,evaluation
+
+# Terminal 3
+celery -A worker.tasks:celery_app beat --loglevel=WARNING --schedule=./data/celerybeat-schedule
+```
+
+Use Compose for the full application on Windows. Pydantic reads service settings from `.env`; for native launches, export any `STREAMLIT_THEME_*` values into the process environment separately if you want the Compose theme. Stop competing Compose application workers/schedulers when switching to a fully native application workflow against the same database.
+
+## Operations and persistence
+
+### Applying changes
+
+| Change | Action |
+| --- | --- |
+| Source code, dependency files, or added/edited evaluation JSON | Rebuild images and recreate application services |
+| `.env` only | Recreate application services so they receive the new environment |
+| Uploaded documents through the UI | Wait for background indexing; no image rebuild |
+| Embedding configuration | Recreate services, then create/repopulate a compatible collection |
+| README or screenshot changes only | No running-service restart required |
+
+Source files and evaluation JSON are copied into the image; they are not bind-mounted by the supplied Compose file.
+
+```powershell
+# After code or dataset changes
+docker compose up -d --build web worker scheduler
+
+# After environment-only changes
+docker compose up -d --force-recreate web worker scheduler
+```
+
+`docker compose restart` restarts existing containers; it does not rebuild code or refresh environment values from a modified `.env`. Changing dataset configuration does not itself request an evaluation. Existing historical runs retain their stored reports.
+
+### Health and logs
+
+```powershell
+docker compose ps
+docker compose exec web python -m src.cli health
+docker compose logs --tail 100 web worker scheduler migrate
+```
+
+The UI also pings workers. LLM status **Configured (not probed)** means configuration/circuit state was checked, not that an actual model request succeeded. Recent errors are local to the current application process; consult container logs for worker failures.
+
+### Persistent data
+
+| Named volume | Contents |
+| --- | --- |
+| `postgres_data` | Collections, document metadata, chunks, vectors, evaluation reports, schema version |
+| `redis_data` | Redis AOF data, cached values, broker and control state |
+| `app_data` | Uploaded files, model cache, evaluation summaries, scheduler state |
+
+```powershell
+docker compose stop
+docker compose start
+```
+
+Stopping or recreating containers preserves these volumes. Back up PostgreSQL and uploaded files together before upgrades or data changes; keep credentials separately protected. No automated backup/restore workflow is included. Changing `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in `.env` does not rotate the password of an already initialized PostgreSQL volume.
+
+`docker compose down -v` deletes named volumes and is destructive; it is not a routine restart command. The UI's document/collection deletion also removes the corresponding stored data.
+
+## Troubleshooting
+
+| Symptom | Check or next step |
+| --- | --- |
+| Docker cannot connect | Start Docker Desktop/Engine and ensure Linux containers are selected |
+| Configuration is incomplete | Compare required values with `.env.example`; recreate services after editing `.env` |
+| Database unavailable | Check `db` health, migration logs, published ports, and credentials; initialized volumes keep their original password |
+| Upload/evaluation stays pending | Confirm both `worker` and `scheduler` are running; dispatch occurs every 30 seconds and queued work shares one worker |
+| Document status is failed | Inspect its issue code and worker logs, resolve the file/provider problem, then use **Retry** |
+| Only four chunks for the microgrid PDF | Expected at the example settings: all four short pages are preserved |
+| A PDF has no usable text | Supply a text-searchable, unlocked PDF; perform OCR before uploading scanned content |
+| A supported question abstains | Check the selected collection, indexed status, source text, and request-detail reason; evaluate relevance settings instead of assuming the model is unavailable |
+| Model temporarily unavailable | Check credentials, model/endpoint compatibility, provider quota, circuit state, and configured fallback availability |
+| First question is slow | Model loading/downloads and cold caches add latency; compare later requests and cache-hit state |
+| New evaluation JSON is not used | Set `EVAL_DATASET_PATH`, rebuild the image, and recreate the worker as well as the web service |
+| Evaluation fails with validation error | Ensure required filenames are indexed in the selected collection and its embedding fingerprint matches |
+| High recall but lower citation scores | Review source labels and PDF whitespace; retrieval recall, quote matching, and semantic correctness are different measurements |
+| RAGAS results are missing | Check the opt-in flag, judge endpoint/model/key, dependencies, and stored report; the UI exposes only the core metrics |
+| Embedding configuration changed | Create a collection indexed with the current embedding configuration |
+| Full tests fail on `dataset_full.json` | Resolve the legacy missing-fixture assertion described in [Development and testing](#development-and-testing) |
+
+## Security and data handling
+
+- Uploaded documents, user questions, and history are untrusted data. The application does not execute uploaded content or give the answer model shell/browser tools.
+- Extension/MIME/signature checks, extraction limits, archive restrictions, and filename/storage-path validation reject common malformed inputs. These checks are not antivirus scanning or a fully sandboxed parser.
+- Injection-pattern checks complement role-separated prompts, bounded context, and citation validation. They can have false positives and do not guarantee resistance to every obfuscated attack or poisoned source.
+- Answers and source excerpts use Streamlit plain-text rendering to avoid activating document-supplied HTML, remote images, or links.
+- Collection-scoped rate limits use a session principal and Redis atomic counters. They do not replace authentication or identity-bound abuse prevention.
+- Remote LLMs receive questions, bounded history, and selected evidence. Remote embedding providers receive text being embedded. Optional RAGAS sends evaluation content to its judge. Local storage does not imply that all inference is local.
+- Application telemetry allowlists operational metadata and drops raw documents, questions, answers, credentials, and exception messages. Optional Langfuse receives this filtered application telemetry; this does not define independent third-party SDK logging behavior.
+- `.env` is excluded from Git and the image build context. Do not publish credentials or private uploaded files in screenshots, test fixtures, or documentation.
+
+The Compose ports bind to loopback by default. Before public or multi-user deployment, add authentication, collection authorization, identity-based limits, TLS, parser isolation, malware scanning, backup/restore procedures, and appropriate infrastructure controls. Collection filtering is not a substitute for access control.
+
+## Known limitations
+
+- Exact-excerpt answers may be less fluent and can abstain on valid questions requiring synthesis, calculations, or relationships across passages.
+- PDF extraction does not perform OCR or reconstruct all visual table relationships. Partially scanned files can contain unextracted pages; DOCX page locations depend on stored metadata/breaks rather than a layout engine.
+- English full-text search and the configured model choices affect language/domain coverage. Long natural-language keyword queries can be restrictive because `plainto_tsquery` combines remaining terms conjunctively.
+- Passage scoring reduces long-chunk dilution, but unusually token-dense text can exceed the bounded window budget. Thresholds and sigmoid scores need domain evaluation.
+- The shown evaluation has only ten document questions and imperfect outcomes. Filename/heading recall is coarse for this PDF; exact-whitespace and lexical metrics are not semantic correctness measures.
+- UI evaluation uses one globally configured dataset and the same worker pool as ingestion. Stored reports do not currently snapshot the full dataset and model configuration for reproducible historical comparisons.
+- Vector retrieval is exact search; no HNSW/IVFFlat vector index is configured. The schema includes a full-text GIN index.
+- There is no user authentication, durable chat-history store, in-place embedding-model migration UI, GPU provisioning in Compose, or automated backup system.
+- Dependency files specify version ranges rather than a fully locked environment. Model behavior and timings can vary across installations and provider changes.
+

# RAG Generator

A document question-answering workspace with separate knowledge bases, hybrid retrieval, cited answers, and an explicit evaluation workflow. Upload **PDF, DOCX, TXT, or Markdown**, ask questions about the selected collection, and inspect the supporting source excerpts.

Built with **Python 3.11+, Streamlit, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Redis, and Celery**. Streamlit handles presentation; ingestion, retrieval, providers, security, caching, and evaluation live in separate service modules.

The application quotes supported passages and abstains when it cannot establish enough evidence. It is intended for a trusted local workspace; authentication and public multi-user hosting are not implemented.

![Knowledge Bases dashboard with the indexed microgrid PDF](images/kb_dashboard.png)

## Contents

- [Features](#features)
- [Architecture](#architecture)
- [How the RAG pipeline works](#how-the-rag-pipeline-works)
- [Quick start with Docker](#quick-start-with-docker)
- [Using the application](#using-the-application)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Evaluation](#evaluation)
- [Application screenshots](#application-screenshots)
- [Development and testing](#development-and-testing)
- [Operations and persistence](#operations-and-persistence)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
- [Security and data handling](#security-and-data-handling)
- [Known limitations](#known-limitations)
- [Project structure](#project-structure)
- [Further documentation](#further-documentation)

## Features

| Capability | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Separate knowledge bases | Collection-scoped documents, retrieval, caches, and evaluation results |
| Background ingestion | File validation, extraction, page/heading metadata, token chunking, indexing |
| Hybrid search | Cosine vector search and English full-text search combined with Reciprocal Rank Fusion |
| Passage reranking | Local cross-encoder scores overlapping passages inside candidate chunks |
| Grounded answers | Structured claims, validated source IDs, supporting quotes, and citations |
| Safe outcomes | Answered, abstained, rejected, and temporarily unavailable responses |
| Model reliability | Configurable primary/fallback LLMs, bounded transient retries, circuit counters |
| Cost controls | Embedding/answer caches and limits on retrieval, context, history, and generation |
| Evaluation | Document-specific datasets, core metrics, optional RAGAS judge |
| Observability | Request details, service checks, filtered application logs, optional Langfuse |

HR policies and the microgrid guide are sample/reference fixtures. Application services are not restricted to either domain.

## Architecture

### Services and dependencies

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Browser["Browser"] --> Web["Streamlit web service"]
    Web --> Services["Python application services"]
    Services --> PG[("PostgreSQL + pgvector")]
    Services --> Files[("Uploaded files")]
    Services --> Redis[("Redis: broker, caches, limits, circuits")]
    Services --> RAG["RAG pipeline"]
    RAG --> PG
    RAG --> Embeddings["Embedding provider: local or remote"]
    RAG --> Reranker["Local cross-encoder"]
    RAG --> LLM["Primary LLM and configured fallbacks"]
    Beat["Celery Beat: every 30 seconds"] --> Redis
    Redis --> Worker["Celery worker"]
    Worker --> PG
    Worker --> Files
    Worker --> Embeddings
    Worker --> Eval["Evaluation service"]
    Eval --> RAG
    Eval -. "Optional" .-> Judge["RAGAS judge endpoint"]
    Services --> Telemetry["Filtered application events"]
    Worker --> Telemetry
    Telemetry --> Logs["Structured JSON logs"]
    Telemetry -. "Optional" .-> Langfuse["Langfuse"]
```

The database holds durable job status. Celery Beat schedules a dispatcher through Redis; the worker reads pending database jobs and queues ingestion/evaluation tasks. Uploading or requesting evaluation does not execute that background work in Streamlit.

| Compose service | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `web` | Streamlit UI and synchronous question answering |
| `worker` | Ingestion and evaluation queues; concurrency one in the supplied configuration |
| `scheduler` | Celery Beat schedule for dispatch and recovery |
| `migrate` | One-shot database bootstrap, pgvector extension, full-text index |
| `db` | PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector |
| `redis` | Broker, caches, rate limits, and LLM circuit state |

Database/Redis health checks gate startup. `migrate` must complete before application services start; its successfully exited container is normal.

### Data model and isolation

| Entity | Stored information |
| --- | --- |
| Collection | UUID, name, revision, embedding-configuration fingerprint |
| Document | Collection UUID, filename, MIME, content hash, storage key, status, attempts, chunk count |
| Chunk | Collection/document UUIDs, source text, page, heading, ordinal, content hash, embedding |
| Evaluation run | Collection UUID, run UUID, status, report JSON, error code |

Raw files live under collection/document UUID paths in shared storage. PostgreSQL holds document metadata, chunks, vectors, and evaluation results. Redis stores disposable caches and operational state. Conversation history is held in the Streamlit session; there is no durable chat-history database table.

Every search filters by `collection_id` and indexed-document status. Composite foreign keys prevent cross-collection chunk ownership. Duplicate file content within a collection is rejected. Atomic chunk publication increments the collection revision, and embedding fingerprints prevent incompatible vector configurations from being mixed.

## How the RAG pipeline works

### 1. Validate and index documents

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant UI as Streamlit
    participant Ingest as Ingestion service
    participant Store as File storage
    participant DB as PostgreSQL
    participant Jobs as Scheduler and worker
    participant Embed as Cached embeddings
    User->>UI: Upload into selected collection
    UI->>Ingest: Validate file and collection
    Ingest->>Ingest: Extract text; reject invalid or duplicate content
    Ingest->>Store: Store file under UUID key
    Ingest->>DB: Create pending document
    Ingest-->>UI: Queued
    Jobs->>DB: Discover job; acquire document lock
    Jobs->>Store: Read uploaded file
    Jobs->>Jobs: Revalidate, extract, and chunk
    Jobs->>Embed: Reuse cache or compute vectors
    Jobs->>DB: Publish chunks; mark indexed; increment revision
    UI->>DB: Refresh document status
```

Validation checks extension, MIME type, signature, size, page limits where available, and usable extracted text. DOCX processing bounds archive expansion and rejects macros and embedded objects. Encrypted PDFs and documents without usable text are rejected. **OCR is not built in.**

Chunking uses tiktoken, preserves page/heading boundaries, and prefers paragraph endings where possible. The example target is **600 tokens with 100-token overlap**; short sections remain shorter. PDF headings are not generally inferred from visual typography, and table cells may become consecutive text lines.

The four-page microgrid PDF correctly produces **four page chunks** at the example settings. Chunk count alone does not establish whether extraction succeeded.

Advisory locks, uniqueness constraints, and atomic publication make duplicate job delivery idempotent. Already indexed documents are skipped. Recoverable jobs have bounded attempts; **Retry** resets a failed document after its underlying issue is resolved.

### 2. Retrieve and generate a cited answer

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q["Question and selected collection"] --> V["Rate limit, validate, check embedding fingerprint"]
    V --> C{"Valid answer cache hit?"}
    C -->|Yes| Cached["Return cached cited answer"]
    C -->|No| E["Embed search query"]
    E --> VS["Scoped vector search"]
    E --> KS["Scoped keyword search"]
    VS --> RRF["Reciprocal Rank Fusion"]
    KS --> RRF
    RRF --> Rank["Rerank bounded passages"]
    Rank --> Gate["Relevance, injection checks, context budget"]
    Gate --> Enough{"Usable evidence?"}
    Enough -->|"No: first retrieval"| Rewrite["One query rewrite"]
    Rewrite --> E
    Enough -->|"No: second retrieval"| Abstain["Safe no-answer response"]
    Enough -->|Yes| Gen["Generate structured claims through reliable LLM"]
    Gen --> Valid{"Claims and citations valid?"}
    Valid -->|"No: first generation"| Retry["One stricter generation attempt"]
    Retry --> Gen
    Valid -->|"No: second generation"| Abstain
    Valid -->|Yes| Revision{"Collection revision unchanged?"}
    Revision -->|Yes| Answer["Return citations and cache grounded answer"]
    Revision -->|No| Abstain
```

**Hybrid retrieval:** pgvector cosine distance supplies semantic candidates. PostgreSQL English `to_tsvector`, `plainto_tsquery`, and `ts_rank_cd` supply keyword candidates. Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines positions using `sum(1 / (60 + rank))`, deduplicated by chunk UUID; it does not average incompatible raw scores.

**Passage reranking:** a local cross-encoder uses its own tokenizer to score overlapping passages. Each original chunk receives its highest passage score, transformed by a sigmoid. Defaults are **180 passage tokens, 40 overlap, at most 16 passages per candidate**. Capped windows are spread across the source. Generation and citations retain original text and provenance. This improves scoring of facts inside PDF pages without re-embedding existing collections.

**Grounding:** the LLM returns JSON claims with text, a chunk UUID, and a quote. Validation checks source membership, matching claim/quote text, source support, and unsafe patterns. A whitespace-normalized fallback accommodates extracted line breaks. The system favors excerpts over free-form paraphrasing or synthesis. Quoting an operator procedure is allowed; executing document instructions is not.

**Safe outcomes:** insufficient evidence or unsupported generated claims produce an abstention. A document explicitly stating that a topic is unspecified can support a cited explanation of that boundary. Confidence comes from selected reranker scores; it is not a calibrated probability or truth guarantee.

### 3. Keep work bounded

| Control | Example or enforced limit |
| --- | --- |
| Vector / keyword candidates | 20 / 20 maximum |
| Reranked candidates | 10 maximum |
| Context chunks | Up to 5 by default; configurable cap 4–6, with fewer allowed when evidence is weak |
| Context / output budget | 3,500 / 1,200 tokens in the example |
| Retrieval attempts / query rewrites | At most 2 / 1 |
| Answer-generation attempts | At most 2 |
| LLM attempts per configured model, per operation | At most 3 |
| History / claims | Up to 6 prior messages in the example / at most 8 claims |

The LLM wrapper retries transient timeouts, connection failures, HTTP 429, and HTTP 5xx with exponential backoff and jitter. Non-transient errors are not retried on the same model. Ordered fallback can use an alternate model on the primary endpoint and an alternate provider. Safety refusals stop fallback. Redis circuit counters temporarily skip repeatedly failing providers. Embeddings and indexing have separate failure paths; the LLM retry wrapper does not wrap all services.

Embedding keys include collection, embedding configuration, query/document purpose, and hashed content. Answer keys include collection revision, normalized question, pipeline/model configuration, and bounded history. Only grounded answers are cached. Document changes advance revisions; deletion also clears collection caches. The same question with different history may miss the cache.

## Quick start with Docker

### Prerequisites

- Docker Desktop with Linux containers, or Docker Engine and the Compose plugin on Linux.
- Internet for the first build/model downloads and any remote providers.
- Memory and disk space for PyTorch, models, database, and documents; requirements depend on model choices. The image installs CPU PyTorch.
- A working remote LLM configuration or a reachable Ollama server with the configured model available.

Run commands from the repository root. Examples use PowerShell unless marked otherwise.

### 1. Configure the environment

```powershell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

Copy only on first setup; preserve an existing `.env`. Before starting:

1. Replace `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and use the matching password in host-side `DATABASE_URL`. URL-encode credentials containing URL-special characters in that URL.
2. Set the primary LLM key/model/endpoint for your selected provider.
3. Review the example Ollama fallback. Run it separately, or disable the alternate provider with `LLM_FALLBACK_PROVIDER=`.
4. Choose embeddings; remote embeddings require their endpoint, key, and matching dimension.
5. Select the evaluation dataset for your documents when you are ready to evaluate.

[.env.example](.env.example) contains configurable deployment examples, not availability guarantees for specific models. Keep credentials in environment configuration; never commit `.env`.

### 2. Build and start

```powershell
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose ps
```

Open [http://localhost:8501](http://localhost:8501), or the port configured through `APP_PORT`. Compose supplies internal database/Redis URLs using container hostnames; native Python uses the URLs in `.env`.

First indexing may load a local embedding model. The first question in each application process loads the reranker. The model cache persists in Docker's shared `app_data` volume.

### 3. Add documents

For the microgrid workflow, create a collection and upload [microgrid_operations_and_response_guide.pdf](tests/fixtures/microgrid_operations_and_response_guide.pdf). Wait for `indexed`, then try:

- What is the normal battery state-of-charge range?
- What should an operator do if battery state of charge falls below 35%?
- What is the exact purchase price of the backup generator?

The last question tests abstention because that price is not specified.

Alternatively, queue the synthetic HR sample collection:

```powershell
docker compose exec web python -m src.cli seed-demo
```

The command queues files from `sample_docs/hr_policies/` and prints the collection UUID. Dispatch happens every 30 seconds; completion also depends on worker load and providers.

| Page | Workflow |
| --- | --- |
| **Knowledge Bases** | Create/select a collection, upload files, inspect indexing/chunk counts, retry failures, delete documents or collections |
| **Ask Questions** | Ask about the selected collection; inspect citations, confidence, timing, and request details |

## Evaluation

Evaluation is explicit and separate from chat. UI runs are stored in PostgreSQL and queued for Celery. CLI runs execute directly and do not create dashboard run records.

### Datasets

| Dataset | Cases | Required collection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [HR](evals/dataset.json) | 10 | All five indexed files from `sample_docs/hr_policies/` |
| [Microgrid](evals/microgrid_dataset.json) | 10: 8 answerable, 2 unanswerable | Indexed microgrid PDF with its expected filename |
